title: Nickerson's violin and tough kids who made students play
summary: A found violin is discussed, then Dejan describes gangs who made Nickerson's students play in the street and how his brother and he were spared.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Yeah. I started to say, two years ago when Fess and I were out in California, we stayed at Johnny St. Cyr, and he had an old violin. It was in about twenty pieces. That's still over there. I never did put it together. But he said he picked it up in the garbage can and it had belonged to some Nickerson who played violin. And Fess says that was a nephew or something like that, or son of the one he took from that

thing. Well, yeah, well it couldn't be. The one that I was taking, that's what he had, was something called Dalton. I think it was Dalton. And he was, I think he's learned him music, but I don't guess that that viol would be, might be for Professor Nixon I know.
Might have been the man who studied with him.

I think so. I think that's what it would be. Because he had a lot of students, he turned some very good scholars out. Just like I said, my brother was a kid and he could play violin very good. And this boy Benny Harmon, with Leffier, he went to California and played with some white man, I don't know who or where, but I haven't seen him since. He was very, very good. In them days the boys was, they didn't carry knives and things like that, but they had little gangs and when they'd come take lessons at Professor Nickerson, they would make some of the boys take their instrument out and play for them. Right there in the grass, he said, I haven't learned anything yet, they'd say. Well play with your loins, learn the lessons, play the scale, anything. Well my brother and I would come along now, you can hear him say, it's Charlie's brother, don't mess with them.
Some of the tough kids up in the Irish channel used to do that too.

Well I was at the corner club, on 2nd and Russo, and it's like I tell you, I knew a lot of them fellas, in the commercial district, see, because on Saturdays I used to deliver bills for my daddy, you know, in places that he did business with I delivered him the bills. And a lot of them fellas knew my daddy from around the commercial district, but they never, so they never did make us do that. But they used to make the boys take, when they come from playing up in Irish town, take the instruments around, play us a tune man. Right there in the street, yeah, play a tune. Well if they go and act nice and play a tune, the instruments wouldn't get broke up or nothing, you know, so if they act nice and play a tune then they could go, you see.
Yeah, otherwise there were a tough bunch of them.
